_about: Chassis. Not classes: any silhouette, any component in any slot. Numbers sit at the scale of tens, magnitudes and not steps (any whole number; docs/rules.md). movespeed is the move in tens: a normal hex costs 10, a fast one 5, and a slow hex can always be entered and ends the move; which ground is which word is the way of moving among traits (tracked, walker, wheeled, hover, flyer; exactly one), bible section 4. size is the machine's class by mass (light, medium, heavy, assault), which sets how big it is drawn on the map and in the skirmish (bible section 7). armour is taken off every blow that lands on bare hull, flat, so small hits bounce off a heavy machine (a standing shield blocks a blow whole; nothing bleeds through). recharge_field is shield regained each battlefield phase spent out of combat; in a fight shield comes only from components (never a free refill, so withdrawing is not a reset). cooling is heat shed at the start of every skirmish turn (0 if absent): venting is a tactic, but a round of ballistics or shields is a way of cooling too. tier is the chassis's tier, 1 to 3 (bible section 10, the ledger, 7 October): power and complexity, never the maker, so any maker may field a tier three and the capital's maker fields no tier one; a run starts with tier-one chassis, and a component's tier follows the lowest tier of chassis that stock it. hardpoints is the number of free slots (and of hp_<n> pins on the model); module_slots is how many modules the chassis carries (bible section 10: a number of the chassis, never bought; two as a rule, three on the Clydesdale as its identifying feature; the runner may move the baseline for some or all); fixed lists the components built into the chassis (always on the die, never removed, no hardpoint used); loadout is the components fitted to the hardpoints by default, and a hardpoint left empty is an entry on the die that does nothing. Every component is one entry, so die size is fixed count plus hardpoints. passive is zero or one object: name and description are shown (the codex prints NAME: description), effects are what the engine runs, at most three, one idea (an upside and its cost count as one passive); the validator refuses effects the engine cannot execute. Shown to the player: codex (the inspect entry, combat and hangar), flavour (an in-world quote), the passive's name and description. design is internal and never shown: fantasy (pitch, inspiration, homages), niche (the role it is meant to fill). Makers are placeholders.

makers.name: Minerva Heavy Works
makers.style: Armour first. Everything is a tank, even the ones with legs.
makers.voice: Maintenance manual. Terse, exact, proud of tolerances.

makers.name: Kestrel Dynamics
makers.style: Fast, fragile, over-tuned. Airframes and interceptors.

makers.name: Wainwright & Sutler
makers.style: Quads and artillery. Old firm, odd designs, everything works.

makers.name: Aphelion
makers.style: Descended from the deep-space programme. Humanoid frames, hover platforms, variable geometry; high-tech suites over light hulls. White with a pearl sheen, red markings.

makers.name: The Arsenal
makers.style: The Council's own R&D house, which need not compete for favour. Heavy walkers, plasma that runs hot, big single hits, burn. Dark steel and gunmetal, black chrome.

entries.name: Honey Badger

design.fantasy: A repurposed mining vehicle, designed to take severe punishment and keep on working. Refurbishments were minimal, basically bolting on weapons and armour, it keeps most of its utilitarian mining machinery flavour.
design.name_clash: Flagged 28 September: the id badger is Heavy Gear's Badger APC and BattleTech's Badger transport; the nickname Honey Badger is nobody's. Kept: the shown name is clear.
design.notes: 6 October (Ryan): the Slug Cannon becomes the Bullion Fragmenter, melee, locked to the Badger as a mining joke; the second Chainsaw Claw goes, so the die is one claw, one fragmenter and three hardpoints (d5) and every face with a model is one face; the right boom's mount is the fragmenter built in, the pins renumbered 1 to 3 (missile box, left gimbal, right gimbal). 9 October, the content revision: the Twin Autoguns became the Blast Door, Minerva's intercept for the starter set, beside the Klaxon (the lure picks foes, the door picks the ally). Later on 9 October Guard came out (Ryan: until we feel we need it), so the Twin Autoguns are back in place of the Blast Door. 10 October (Ryan): Close removed, so the cracked-weapons-go-melee line went with it; the +5 reads the melee tag its two locked weapons carry; the passive is overloaded and is to be reworked around the Chainsaw Claw and the Bullion Fragmenter. Later on 10 October (Ryan): the +5 to melee trimmed too, since a chassis passive that reads a tag asks for every melee component; its two locked weapons are where its identity goes.

entries.codex: The Minerva EX-45L (colloquially nicknamed the "Badger") was popular a mining mech widely praised for its reliability and durability, being designed to operate in the harshest, deepest environments imaginable. Reports exist of Badgers being caught in cave-ins while mining over 5 kilometers underground, only to dig their way out to the surface by nightfall, just in time for drinks with the crew. So naturally, when the Rifts opened, the ever-practical Minerva engineering team's first instinct was to finally give their prized Badger claws, teeth, and as many missiles as it could carry, putting its legendary longevity to work on the battlefield.

passive.name: Reinforced Skeleton
passive.description: Legendary Minervan strength. Components can be cracked but never destroyed.

entries.flavour: Hey Russ, ain't that yer Badger over there, covered in demon innards? I thought they retired the ol' girl!

entries.name: Clydesdale

design.fantasy: A massive, boxy, heavily armoured, and utilitarian quadruped walker, designed to fill whatever niche the team is lacking. Like its namesake, it has four thick legs and carries a massive payload on top.
design.notes: Not sure if this needs a passive, since by lore this probably doesn't want too many locked components. This design is intentionally vanilla, as it's a jack-of-all-trades horse that can mount a ton of stuff, but for gameplay purposes it might need something to prevent it from being actually lame and boring. If we make it unique in that it has a very high number of hardpoints, then a passive ability that helps control roll randomness somehow would probably be appropriate. Decided 28 September: the d9 stays (the die cap is 10 now) and the passive is Battery Director, a free reroll of its own die once a round, die-local so the team gets no knock-on; if it feels thin it gets two, or ten entries. Its identity is capacity, which the hangar will show. Shock Barrage is its advanced piece. 9 October, the content revision: one Twin Autoguns became the Maxigun (three strikes). 9 October: the platings left the dice for modules, so the Ablative Plating became the Blast Door and the Flak Skirt the Incendiary Shells (the artillery quad was weakest alone, and its shields were among its smallest spends).

entries.codex: Surprisingly, or perhaps not, the ever-pragmatic Wainwright & Sutler were the first surviving manufacturer to field a combat walker when the invasion first began. Not knowing the full scope of the threat, the Clydesdale was positioned as a rugged and effective jack-of-all trades, a true workhorse befitting its namesake. A hundred years later, and the original design is still barely changed, its signature W&S simplicity being favourited by pilots and maintenence crews alike. It also serves as an effective training vehicle, as its notoriously poor turning radius results in one less thing for a green pilot to worry about on the battlefield.

passive.name: Battery Director
passive.description: Rerolling only the Clydesdale's die is free once a round, on top of the team's rerolls.

entries.flavour: Pilot manual footnotes: Most of the Clydesdale controls are just for show. The only ones you really need are accelerate and alpha strike.

entries.name: Kite

design.fantasy: A priority-target interceptor. Designed for speed and firepower and not much else, taking out a key asset and fleeing while its generous shields recharge.
design.name_clash: The id only, since 21 October: sparrowhawk is a Halo Wars gunship and a BattleTech aerospace fighter, and the id stays because ids are never shown. The name's pass (Ryan, 28 September) closed when he renamed the machine the Kite, which clashes with nothing.
design.one_off: Its passive carries four effects, the cap three (Ryan's sketch of 19 October, his go of 21 October): the double, the flat heat, the dark rounds and the kill's tax are one idea in two lines, the double-edged niche definer the one-idea row names.
design.notes: Reworked 21 October on Ryan's go (the bible's Kite row; the brief retired to git): tier two, a d3 of the Pinion Driver locked and two hardpoints, hull 30, shield 40, heat maximum 40, cooling 10, a light flyer at 50; the passive's name kept, its rules the rework's. Its two hardpoints stock placeholders by kind until the stock pass: a cold rolled gun (the Twin Autoguns, standing in for a 15-30 kinetic) and a cold Indirect gun (the Howitzer). Numbers are placeholders.

entries.codex: Shortly into the invasion, it was determined that the masses of zombies, demons, and otherwordly things were, frankly, quite dumb without a guiding intelligence coordinating them. Naturally, Kestrel won the bid to produce a small interceptor aircraft, designed to eliminate priority targets and disengage before getting overwhelmed. However, the weapons package traditionally mounted on such a small frame proved ineffective to the task. It wasn't until one inspired engineer suggested cutting all 'uneccesary' weight from the design that a breakthrough was achieved; Armour, weapon regulators, ejection systems, and padded seats were all deemed frivolous, and their omission skyrocketed the Sparrowhawk to excel in its role.

passive.name: Disabled Weapon Regulators
passive.description: Premium Kestrel "feature." Every weapon fires at double its printed number, 10 hotter, and goes dark for two rounds. Each attack that kills makes its shots 5 hotter for the fight.

entries.flavour: There's lighting a fire under your ass, and then there's piloting a Kite. I suggest a cold plunge before you strap in.

entries.name: Baboon

design.fantasy: A long-armed, stubby-legged plantigrade walker with a high tech suite of weapons and equipment mounted on its backpack. Not fast or heavily armoured, it specializes in battlefield control through status effects and high-tech equipment with complex effects.
design.notes: Numbers and designation are Claude's first fill (26 September), the passive and stock re-cut 28 September, all Ryan's to move. Stock is Aphelion's generic kit (two Umbra Projectors on the shoulders, two Pulse Vacillators and the Zenith Emitter on the fists, a Radiator Sail); the Corona Shield is a unique unlock now, not stock. A d7 since 30 September (Ryan: the fists rest on the ground and carry the guns, two mounts a hand): the Halo Shield was dropped, since Pocket Paradox pays for missing shield and a shield component fights it. The fixed pods carry the Solar Flare Array so the passive has a status to read alone. 9 October, the content revision (Aphelion's support most): the two Pulse Vacillators became the Differentiation Probe and the Polarity Projector, and the Radiator Sail the Phased Sublimator, so its stock carries a disrupt, a shock that feeds the Pocket Paradox, and a cleanse. 10 October (Ryan): the Pocket Paradox is a meter, not a chance (a chance to stun is game-winning when it lands and nothing when it does not): an application of any other status adds a Paradox, of any number of stacks, so several components must fire or one hit must carry several statuses; at three the foe is Suppressed. Paradox is a status like any other and never decays; it never feeds itself (the Suppressed it causes is not counted). The missing-shield clause is dropped, so a shield no longer fights the passive and the stock may take one again (the stock pass). 11 October (Ryan): stays tier one, with basic components in the stock pass. Renamed the Kite on 21 October (the Sparrowhawk until then; Ryan: the old name was a BattleTech aircraft's, given a pass as a coincidence, and the pass closes; the Kite is the light, agile raptor that twists on its forked tail, the acrobat). The id stays.
design.name_clash: Was the Mandrill (a BattleTech 'Mech that looks like ours); renamed the Baboon 28 September, Ryan's pick: a funny name for a funky machine Aphelion thought was cool. Gelada was too obscure for pilots to have coined, Silverback implied a fighter. Baboon is itself the Clan designation of BattleTech's Howler (a 20-ton light 'Mech); Ryan keeps it, a designation-tier clash like the Goshawk's.

entries.codex: Looking like a cross between an orangutan and a troll, what the Baboon lacks in speed or endurance it more than makes up for with high-tech Aphelion technomagic. After the rifts first opened (and upended everything mankind knew about the laws of physics and the nature of the universe), Aphelion set to work assimilating the torrent of new data, developing experimental countermeasures at a frenetic pace. One unlucky researcher managed to knock out his past self using a localized pocket paradoxical time loop. The effect was quickly weaponized and a frame built to lug the heavy device in into battle, nicknamed the "Baboon" in the researcher's memory.

passive.name: Pocket Paradox
passive.description: A localized paradoxical time loop, weaponized. When a foe gains a status other than Paradox, it gains a stack of Paradox; at three its past self knocks it out (Suppressed), and the Paradox clears.

design.fantasy: A squat, heavily armoured walker with short, thick legs, its back bristling with weaponry from shielded ports that can seal for additional protection. The cockpit is tucked under the front armour, providing reduced visibility but extra protection. It seals: the ports shutter, the shell goes dark, and everything shoots the shell.
design.notes: Probably needs taunt effects on one or more locked or stock components. Wants a retaliate ability that  damages and/or causes status on foes that hit hull, but not sure if that is a passive or component that needs activating. Decided 28 September: the tankiest machine in the game, its toughness in the numbers and the passive and never in locked plating, so the free die is the player's. Faraday Hull is retaliation as a debuff, not thorns (thorns scales with enemy blows and inverts horde against boss); the locked Faraday Shutters are its taunt and extend the shock to blocked blows; the crack threshold needs no help at this hull. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. 6 October: its Slug Cannon slot carries the Slugthrower, Minerva's new default gun, since the cannon became the Badger's fixed Bullion Fragmenter. 9 October, the content revision: the Ablative Plating became the Shoring Jack (Braced on itself or an ally). 11 October (Ryan): the discharge a Shocked striker paid went (it was the larger share of the passive's strength against a horde, measured: the lone Armadillo 85 and 92 to 64 and 85); Shocked is the setup alone. 20 October (Ryan's go on the form-changing tank, his framework of 15 October): the Faraday Hull and the Lockdown Shutters leave it (the Hull's idea waits on the echidna); Lockdown is the passive, the Cryo Flinger pair its locked piece, the four weapon ports its four hardpoints, base armour 5 so the seal reads 15 in all. Every heat number is a placeholder ahead of the heat rework; the stock (the Blast Door its shield, the Blowout Stack its vent) is the stock pass's.

passive.name: Lockdown
passive.description: A shield it spends on itself seals it: armour +10, its own cooling stopped, 15 hotter at the end of each turn. A vent or a damaging weapon opens it.

design.fantasy: An unstoppable assault tank, complete with front rams and plows, designed for breaching reinforced emplacements - or plowing over and through fodder monsters.
design.notes: Passive should be something about being able to access the backline, or some other vanguard-punch-through ability. Decided 28 September: a diver, not a bruiser (that is the Badger). Juggernaut Drive puts overwhelm on every attack, so a kill's spare damage reaches the back rank from any gun; the locked Breaching Plow is its one melee hit, cleaving, and carries the front armour as its own passive. Five hardpoints since 30 September (Ryan): two parallel turret guns, a mount on the turret's top and one on each rear quarter; a second Slug Cannon fills the turret pair. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. 6 October: its two Slug Cannon slots carry the Slugthrower, Minerva's new default gun, since the cannon became the Badger's fixed Bullion Fragmenter. 9 October: the platings left the dice for modules (Ryan: a hardpoint carries something mounted; armour slapped on is a module), so the Ablative Plating became the Blast Door, Minerva's mounted shield.

passive.name: Juggernaut Drive
passive.description: Momentum carries through. Damage past a kill spills into the rank behind, from any weapon.

design.fantasy: A fast, agile, and lightly armoured skirmisher, able to skim in and out of fights with ease. It's signature ability allows it to serve as both a potent scout and harasser before getting away with minimal damage.
design.notes: Decided 28 September: the passive as Ryan wrote it, resolved per ally with a flat chance and no new UI: the Prairie Dog is always out before the enemy strikes, each ally rolls an even chance to slip out with it, and a blow aimed at a covered machine is lost rather than retargeted. The locked Flakshot Repeater makes its round shoot, roll again, shoot, leave; Incendiary Shells because it leaves them burning (burning carried between fights is on the ideas list). Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. 8 October (Ryan, the redesigned round, bible sections 4, 5 and 7): the scout that slips around the fights; elusive, a hunter never picks it, so it is never in a fight it did not choose and works behind the horde. The Static-screen Projector is gone (the guaranteed enemy turn); its locked gun is to carry the disorder keyword in its place and the Flak Skirt is to go with the niche, both not yet done. 8 October, later (Ryan): elusive is a passive, not a trait, since no other machine will carry it; named the Track-Dispersing Tyres (Ryan, 9 October). The model lost its side skirts, bash bars and drops the same day, and rides higher over its wheels (Ryan: the fast scout, a dune buggy's flair). Claude's recommendation, open with Ryan: the Flakshot Repeater stays as it is (a rapid gun suits a light machine that finishes its own fights fast) and the disorder keyword is dropped (it pays in team fights, which an elusive car rarely joins); the Flak Skirt is stock in a free hardpoint, never the design. 9 October: the platings left the dice for modules, so the Flak Skirt became the Laminar Deflector, a mounted shield (W&S has none of its own yet), since the skirt was a quarter of its spends alone. Ryan's go, 19 October (the bible's Prairie Dog row; the brief retired to git: git show f5a085a:docs/briefs/ws_prairie_dog.md): the fight half is the Flakshot Repeater's, which sprays a flat 5 and lays Flak 2 (planned), the maker's on-hit, so the car is the maker's softener: it skims in, sprays the rank, and the four cash it; the map half stays what it is. Claude's Spread-alone shape (a rule reading no ally in the fight) retired with the go. The stock is the stock pass's (the basic shield for the Deflector). The roster's want of a fast machine that fights alone (section 4) stays open. The pivot, Ryan's go of 21 October ("Prairie dog is locked, go flak 2 spread for now. Passive carries the damage reduction."): the Repeater loses Rapid (Direct, flat 5, Spread, Flak 2), and the passive gains its fight half beside the map rule, 5 less from any foe carrying Flak, whoever laid it (Ryan, 20 October: on the passive and not the piece, so the Cottonmouth's shells and any Flak weapon the car carries cover it). Built as a damage-taken effect conditioned on the striker's status (attacker_status), inert until Flak lands; the passive stays built, so the car stays dealable.

passive.name: Track-Dispersing Tyres
passive.description: Treads cut to scuff out their own trail as they roll. No hunter ever picks the Prairie Dog as its prey, and a foe carrying Flak hits it 5 lighter.

design.fantasy: A small, nimble, lightly armoured vehicle designed to support heavy armour in combat. Able to stealthily avoid combat until its allies are in position for a flanking or pincer attack, then capitalize on openings in combat.
design.name_clash: Kept (Ryan, 29 September). Dingo is a Heavy Gear Northern gear, an obscure resin-era release in a niche property and a biped, so no silhouette resemblance; the Bundeswehr's ATF Dingo, a four-wheeled armoured car, is the closer match and the homage W&S's register is built on. Say Dingo and people picture the dog: the coincidence tier.
design.notes: Decided 28 September: stealth is a trait, not a passive (like flyer): it controls no ground and joins a fight only when an ally is in it or when it stopped a pack in its path, so it waits in the wings and never fights alone unless run into. The passive is the other half of Ryan's Adaptive Camouflage, the flanking bonus, as Tactical Databank. The locked Megataser Harpoon is a cheap pin for the foe an ally is about to eat; Coolant Dump because it can be spent on a friend. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. 8 October (Ryan, the redesigned round, bible sections 4, 5 and 7): stealth is gone; the Dingo is tireless, two actions a turn, the pack animal that drifts between fights, its Tactical Databank making its second action count in an ally's fight. It can be hunted, and dies if it strays from the pack. 8 October, later (Ryan): the second action is the Dingo's passive (named the Retrograde Flywheel, 9 October, by Ryan: the perfect amount of no-sense), and the Tactical Databank leaves the Dingo to become the game's first module, its name kept (Ryan): "With an ally in the fight, this machine's kinetic weapons roll their maximum" (on_attack, roll_max, when ally_present), for when modules exist (bible section 10). Ryan's go, 19 October (the bible's Dingo row; the brief retired to git: git show 021f075:docs/briefs/ws_dingo.md): a second locked piece, the Combat Translocator (his working name), which picks two foes or a foe and an empty slot and swaps them (the Swap keyword, planned in the vocabulary), tier two with it. The piece lands in content with its engine (a spend that takes two targets, a foe moving between slots), not before: a planned locked piece would keep the Dingo out of the tender and fix the maker's deal on the Prairie Dog, which the tier move is timed to avoid; the tier moves when a Wainwright & Sutler tier one beside the Prairie Dog can be dealt. Its stock beside the harpoon is the stock pass's (the Coolant Dump retires there).

passive.name: Retrograde Flywheel
passive.description: A flywheel that banks the car's momentum between bursts and pays it back out. The Dingo has two actions a turn: it may move and fight, then move and fight again.

design.fantasy: The larger cousin of the Sparrowhawk, trades explosiveness for longevity. Wide downturned wings evoking a hovering predator, weapon mounts mounted under the wings. Double boosters mounted on top of the tail section (similar to an A10 warthog).
design.niche: Hot sustain: shield from its heat, and one blow that fires it all
design.notes: Locked weapon(s) should vent heat and deal increased damage proportional to heat vented. Decided 28 September: split, not stacked. The passive is sustain from heat (Thermal Recoupler regains shield per 10 heat at the start of its turn, the game's first in-fight regen, safe on one chassis) and the locked Afterburner Cannon is the burst that spends it: ride hot for regen or dump for the hit. Damage scaling dropped; the Sparrowhawk owns that. Arc Projector is its advanced piece. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. Renamed the Buzzard on 21 October (the Goshawk until then; Ryan: the old name's pass was an obscure nickname's, and it closes with the Sparrowhawk's; the Buzzard is the big broad-winged raptor that soars and stays, which is what this machine does). The id stays.
design.name_clash: The id only, since 21 October: goshawk is the Inner Sphere designation of the Clan Vapor Eagle (a 55-ton 'Mech), and the id stays because ids are never shown. The name's pass (Ryan, 28 September) closed when he renamed the machine the Buzzard, which clashes with nothing.

passive.name: Thermal Recoupler
passive.description: Heat is not waste. At the start of its turn the Buzzard regains 5 shield for every 10 heat it carries.

design.fantasy: A hulking, neckless, spiked brute. Thick arms made for pummeling. A glowing firey core in its torso that lights up as the mech takes damage and heats up.
design.notes: One or more locked components should grant overheating, or deal self -damage. Decided 28 September: Crucible Capacitor counts blows that reach hull from foes or its own weapons, never overheat burn (that loop has no brake), and the stacks decay as Overheating does; a plain vent is its relief. The locked Gravity Knuckles are volatile, so every punch feeds it, and volatile is the general Arsenal self-damage keyword for later shield and vent faces. Meteor Artillery is its advanced piece. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. 9 October, the content revision: the Plasma Carbine became the Retribution Thurible (Retaliate, so the foes that reach its hull set up its next punch). 9 October: the platings left the dice for modules, so the Ward Plate became the Oblation Ward, the Arsenal's shield paid in hull. 10 October: Close removed, so the Crucible reads the melee tag (its Gravity Knuckles carry it). 10 October (Ryan): the passive in his words, hull damage feeding melee for the skirmish with no Overheating in between; the overheat that heat can cause is hull damage too, which a savvy player works out alone. The Gravity Knuckles lost volatile with it. 12 October (Ryan): the Crucible becomes rage. Taking hull damage, all of it (a blow, a bite of its own, an overheat), banks a rage for the skirmish, and its new locked fists, the Knuckle of Fury, spend one when they strike and the die rolls again, nothing switching off, so the rage is the limit: "it's not a choice, you just get rapid". The +5 melee a stack is gone, rage buying actions only. The Gravity Knuckles left for tier three.

passive.name: Crucible Capacitor
passive.description: Taking hull damage banks a rage, up to 5, for the duration of the skirmish.

design.fantasy: A sinister digitigrade figure, with 4 clawed arms, the middle set which can be used as an additional pair of legs. A low-set snout like cockpit with burning "eyes." Absorbs energy from units it defeats with its 4 signature locked claw weapons, granting permanent overcharge.
design.notes: Needs 4 locked components: melee weapons that grant overcharge on kill. Not sure of name, something sinister about assimilation or draining or attuning or something. Decided 28 September: four locked Soulcutter Talons (devour to grow; execute to finish until 10 October) and four hardpoints, the d8 Ryan wrote as a total. Quintessence Tap keeps the Overcharged stacks for the battle, never the campaign, so the snowball has an end. Arsenal names stay sanctified on their face and sinister on reflection. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. 9 October, the content revision: the Ward Plate became the Oblation Ward (a volatile shield, the Arsenal's premium).

passive.name: Quintessence Tap
passive.description: Overcharged never fades on this machine, whatever granted it, and lasts the battle.

design.fantasy: A flat pearl-white lens of a hull that rides on lift fans sunk flush into its wings and pitches like a helicopter to move. Its heat suite is its weapon: the hotter it runs, the deeper every burn and every buff it lays. The ray's barb is its tail, lit at the tip; its mouth is the lance under the nose.
design.notes: Proposed and decided 2 October (Ryan picked Stingray over Lionfish and Sea Wasp; Lionfish was Claude's lead). The second Aphelion machine, carrying the heat idea weighed and parked when the Baboon's passive was chosen (28 September). Cooling 0 by design: it never cools on its own, the Radiator Sail is its only brake, so every round is a heat decision; heat_max 100 so the suite has five steps to climb. Propulsion by maker (Ryan, 2 October): Aphelion's hovers and aircraft are aquatic, fans and rotors in places, so the Stingray's lift is ducted fans flush in the wing discs; Kestrel keeps the big boosters; the exposed-rotor fan-copter (the Banshee register) is kept free for a later Aphelion flyer, and W&S flyers would be traditional helicopter profiles. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. Ryan, 2 October: five extra Burning at 100 heat is probably silly, and easy to tune; the passive double-dips through Primed (the Primed stacks it lays are deepened, and so are the burns those blows lay), a knob for the runner. 9 October, the content revision: the Pulse Vacillator became the Halo Shield (Ryan the same day: pick the stock by design and balance, never to give a component a home; the Zenith Emitter was its biggest spend alone, the Repeater among its smallest). 9 October (Ryan: a locked component is never a blueprint; that is why it is locked): the Solar Flare Array is the Baboon's locked piece, so the Stingray's hardpoint takes the Incendiary Shells, the plain indirect burn, and the passive keeps a burn to read. 11 October (Ryan): tier one beside the Baboon, both with basic components in the stock pass, though both read as tier two; Aphelion needs more chassis designs.

passive.name: Exothermic Suite
passive.description: Heat is the suite's power. Every stack this machine applies, to a foe, an ally or itself, is one deeper for every 20 heat it carries. Numbed excepted, as always.

design.fantasy: Kestrel's one machine that touches the ground, and so the one Kestrel that can stop a pack. A short deep body in chrome on two boosters far too big for it, stubby wings, tail fins, and the whole front one shield projector, a great faired beak. Kestrel called it a very cool ground-effect escort; pilots took one look and called it the Puffin.
design.notes: Proposed and decided 2 October: the Puffin the bible's makers row wanted (28 September). The slowest Kestrel (Ryan: allowed, since lore-wise they loaded it with tech instead of guns), so movespeed 3; hover, so it skims water and chokes on ruins. Boosters, never fans: Ryan, 2 October, anything but big boosters is off-brand for Kestrel. Passive open: Ryan's lean is an overshield (shield allies past their maximum) with a cost or a second effect; Claude's shape, 2 October, is overshield that fades at the end of the round with the fixed projector pointing outward only, since shield-the-Puffin-every-turn would be a shield-bot. Planned until he decides. The Overcharge Coil gets its first chassis here. Numbers, designation and kit are Claude's fills, Ryan's to move. The passive decided 5 October (Ryan: shield for heat reduced is very effective; no penalty, the die is the brake): Slipstream is a placeholder name, Ryan's to move. The overshield went to the fixed Prow Projector as a rare keyword rather than the passive, by the bible's rule that a passive multiplies what components do and a new mechanic is a component's. Weighed and dropped: Spillover (shield past the Puffin's maximum flowing to an ally; win-more), a received-shield penalty (adds no decision; the one-man show cannot happen on a d5 with the only overshield allies-only). 6 October (Ryan): move 40, the 40 club with the Dingo, Goshawk and Stingray, since a small hovercraft slower than the Dingo felt wrong (the 'slowest Kestrel' line retired; Ryan adjusts the lore); the passive named the Slipstream Projector, extra dumb on purpose, a slipstream given to allies to shed heat by science magic; the fixed shield renamed the Backwash Ionizer. 9 October, the content revision: the Ram-air Scoop became the Wake Diffuser (a rapid vent: the escort cools an ally and acts again). Reworked on Ryan's go, 21 October (his worry of 20 October: toxic and boring; his split, the passive reads heat and the lock is the overshield through it): the Slipstream Projector, its name kept, now grows every shield it spends on an ally by a fifth of the heat that ally carries (one for one at the stock pass's heat scale of 1-20), stocked shields included; the cooling it gave (10 heat shed by whoever it shielded) went as the toxic half, which also fought the heat the new passive rewards. The Backwash Ionizer's base came down from 30 to 10 with it, so the hottest ally at the top of its gauge gets today's 30 and a cold ally 10; no cap, the ratio bounds it. Half the ally's heat is the lever if it plays as a trickle. Cooling is a stock choice now, the vent that shields. The rounds are in git: git show b4dfbe5:docs/briefs/kestrel_puffin.md. Tier one since 21 October (Ryan: comfortable with the reworked Puffin at tier one, to balance the line as the Kite moves to tier two; its identity shows with basics alone, since any shield it spends on an ally grows). Its stock moved with it until the stock pass gives it a tier one's (basics beside the Ionizer), so the Laser Carbine, the Overcharge Coil and the Wake Diffuser read as tier-one pieces and starting blueprints meanwhile.

passive.name: Slipstream Projector
passive.description: A slipstream, projected forward. A shield this machine spends on an ally grows by a fifth of the heat that ally carries.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 14 October: "a unit that sits on the sidelines, waiting to strike. Its opportunistic. We have many scaling threats, but no dedicated tank-buster, which was my inspiration - little spider takes down big thing with venom." A four-legged steampunk walker that does spider-like things (Ryan, 17 October); the lore is his and not written yet.
design.niche: The roster's tank-buster, a team machine at tier two: its blows on a foe looking away lay Vitriol (a share of current hull), the team's Lures, stuns and bare-hulled tank making its windows; its locked Web Bomb binds. Alone it is a plain d5 with a web and loses, which is tier two's shape. It waits on the elites in fights for the venom to matter outside the boss fight.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 18 October, on the design settled in chat 17 and 18 October (the brief retired to git: git show bfa8cf2:docs/briefs/ws_funnel_web.md; the bible's funnel-web row carries the decisions and their reasons). The name, the designation and every number are working placeholders (medium walker, move 30; hull 110, shield 40, armour 5, heat 60, cooling 5, recharge 20; four hardpoints, a d5). The stock is stand-ins until the stock pass: the Maxigun (its first chase piece: strikes are bites), the Howitzer, the Twin Autoguns, the Laminar Deflector. The passive runs since 18 October (lay_status on a foe showing no intent on it, the target_no_intent condition read at the spend before the spend's own riders, each foe reached judged alone, a stack per strike that lands with a number, so a blow of nothing such as its own web is no hit; Vitriol's share tick), its Web Bomb bursts, and the HUD's predator sense shows while its die is held or dragged (RIFTGATE_PREY_DEBUG=1 keeps it on). Its lowforge model landed 19 October (models_low.py's funnel_web; the bible's funnel-web row and its motion table describe it), three cuts in the day on Ryan's notes: a mechanical spider, then a low quad in the BattleTech Scorpion's shape (a war machine: one hull, the legs under the mass, more leg to body, the gear on geometry of its own, practical feet), then the Revenant's and the Arachnotron's legs under a turret (its legs revised on his third notes: down, up and down, a strut dropping from the hub to a low hip so the thigh clears the body), then on his fourth notes the body in W&S's military camp with the side guns pitching only and a creeping walk with the upper legs in it, revised on his fifth (two static bow guns in a widened jaw, the Howitzer alone on the roof, the web launcher in the left pod, the dish on the right; the fore feet's double step and the head's turn cut from the creep; on his sixth the coxae rowing under the solver, a longer stride and a wider carry so the feet stop flicking), the cut that stands, for him to judge running in the hangar.

passive.name: Ambush
passive.description: Its blows on a foe showing no intent on it lay Vitriol: a stack per hit, and at its action the foe loses 5% of its current hull a stack.

design.fantasy: Ryan's revolver (12 October): "Whenever its die rolls, it moves to the next entry instead, in sequence." The six-shooter homage on a chicken walker: a squared cab on two long digitigrade legs, no arms, the revolver drum on the cab's flank clicking round a chamber at every roll. Ryan, 18 October: the first chamber randomized, "like a revolver spinning, the only random factor we're able to inject in an otherwise deterministic chassis". Named by Ryan, 19 October: the flightless bird that kills.
design.niche: The maker's gunslinger, a damage dealer at tier one (Ryan, 18 October: promoted to damage class). Its die never rolls: each fight opens on a random chamber and steps from there, so the plan is adjacency (the shield before the big gun, the Rapid before the chamber it should double) and the team's rerolls are its dial. Every sixth shot counts double; its locked Spin-Up spins the cylinder and primes the next shot. Squishy on purpose (Ryan, 19 October: "we're packing a lot of firepower in it"), so the maker's tender deal holds no front, accepted.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 19 October, on the design settled in chat 18 and 19 October (the brief retired to git: git show 021f075:docs/briefs/ws_revolver.md; the bible's Cassowary row carries the decisions and their reasons). Ryan's names: the Cassowary, the Spin-Up, Spun Up; the passive's name and the designation are Claude's working ones. Every number is a placeholder (medium walker, move 40; hull 80, shield 30, armour 0, heat 60, cooling 5, recharge 20; five hardpoints and the Spin-Up, a six-chamber die). The stock is stand-ins until the stock pass, basics only, in an order that teaches the cycle: the Blast Door and the Coolant Jacket at V and VI, two quiet chambers before the Spin-Up at I and the Howitzer at II. The passive was built 21 October: the die mode (the spin at the fight's start, a step on every roll and reroll, Scramble a true roll, a lock a hold), the sixth-shot count with its six pips under the heat bar, and the next-chamber chip; the hold marks the next chamber in place of a ring, and the hangar's numbered chambers wait on the hangar. No model yet (MechView3D borrows the Badger's); its lowforge model, rig, acts and gait are the asset session's. The Rapid chain's price is the stock pass's (Rapid priced in heat), so its balance waits on that pass and its runner row is a verdict on the bot until the bot plans a cycle.

passive.name: Indexed Cylinder
passive.description: Its die never rolls: each fight opens on a random chamber, and every roll steps it to the next entry in order. Every sixth shot counts double, its damage and the stacks it lays.

design.fantasy: Ryan, 13 October: a simple hovercraft with a deck gun, and everything it fires goes through the deck gun. Ryan, 19 October: "I picture it honestly not as a deck gun, but like a big rotating set of barrels with the guns mounted (invisibly) inside, like a multi shot grenade launcher. We call it a fan boat but the profile is more sophisticated than that, it is still future-tech after all." Named by Ryan, 19 October: the water moccasin, the bayou's snake.
design.niche: The maker's versatility in a third form, of reach (Ryan, 19 October: the Clydesdale's is loadout, the gunship's stats, this one's reach), a tier one that plugs holes in many draft compositions. Every weapon it fires leaves the drum as the drum's Indirect shot with the weapon's own keywords, so a keyword shell of any maker becomes an area shot at any reach; the shape follows the aim (the back rank punched through, the front rank sprayed), so a column or a row is the decision on every shot. It spreads statuses well, which steps on Aphelion's toes and is fine (Ryan: status spread is no monopoly and no complete identity). It locks nothing, as the Clydesdale and the gunship do.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 19 October, on the design settled in chat 18 and 19 October (the brief retired to git: git show 021f075:docs/briefs/ws_fan_boat.md; the bible's Cottonmouth row carries the decisions and their reasons). Ryan's names: the Cottonmouth, the Adaptive Munitions Drum; the designation is Claude's working one. The launcher is the passive's rule, not an entry on the die (Ryan: "the deck gun isn't actually a locked component"): Indirect, flat 15 (Ryan: 15 is ok), heat 10 (Claude's lean over 5, taken 19 October: at 5 under cooling 10 the machine never heats, even firing a Rapid shell twice a turn; the stock pass re-prices it), tagged Ballistic. Every number is a placeholder (light hover, move 50; hull 60, shield 30, armour 0, heat 60, cooling 10, recharge 30; four hardpoints and nothing locked, a d4). The stock is stand-ins until the stock pass: the Incendiary Shells (Burn rides the spray, the passive's lesson), the Ankle Mortar (a plain shot, so the number is the drum's), the Blast Door (equipment fires as itself), the Coolant Jacket. The passive was built 21 October: the rewrite of every weapon spent (rewrite_weapon: the drum's number, reach and heat, one blow, the weapon's keywords, rules and tags kept, Ballistic added, the die showing the shot as it will fire over the foe it is dragged over) and a keyword granted by the target's rank (the target_rank condition); while danger close stands the front-rank spray costs shield, as any Indirect shot at the front does. No model yet (MechView3D borrows the Badger's); for the asset session: a hover hull under a drum, the fitted guns inside the drum, so this is the one machine whose hardpoints show no mounts on the model.

passive.name: Adaptive Munitions Drum
passive.description: Every weapon it fires leaves the drum as the drum's shot: Indirect, 15, heat 10, with the weapon's own keywords. Aimed at the back rank the shot punches through (Penetrate); aimed at the front rank it sprays (Spread).

design.fantasy: Ryan's eight-legged spider whose vents blast a random foe for the heat they shed (12 and 13 October): "a crazy steampunk machine venting everywhere"; 20 October: "it doesn't actually use steam to run, its a future-tech machine. it just kind of behaves like a steampunk device." The whip scorpion sprays when provoked. Named by Ryan, 20 October.
design.niche: The maker's sustained damage dealer at tier two (Ryan, 18 October: promoted to damage class; 20 October: "a sustained dps engine"): heat is its ammunition and every vent is a gun, blasting a random live foe for the heat it takes off. Nothing cools it but its vents (cooling 0), so every point of heat it earns, from its hot guns, its Siphon's lure-all or the Peak's debuffs, stays until a valve opens on it. A heavy body that can detach; its Siphon makes it a partner.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 20 October, on the design settled in chat from 12 October to 20 October (the brief retired to git: git show 4a8ab1d:docs/briefs/ws_boiler.md; the bible's Whip Scorpion row carries the decisions and their reasons). Ryan's names: the Whip Scorpion, the Thermal Ejection Manifold, the Heliographic Siphon, the Thermal Ray; the designation is Claude's working one. Every number is a placeholder (heavy walker, move 20; hull 150, shield 30, armour 10, heat 100, cooling 0, recharge 15; four hardpoints and the Siphon, a d5). The stock is stand-ins until the stock pass: the Thermal Ray (the hot gun), two Coolant Jackets (two valves on a d5), the Maxigun; the Stoker, a W&S piece that Burns a foe and its own firer, is the stock pass's. The passive was built 21 October: the vent rider (vent_blast: the heat a vent takes off its owner as one blow on a random live foe drawn from the seeded stream, through the damage pipeline, armour and the foe's statuses applying; a vent on an ally blasts nothing, an ally's vent on it blasts nothing) and the bot's valuation of it; the forecast on the vent entry is the to-do's. The passive gain of 10 a round (Ryan, 12 October) went on 20 October (too easy: a free blast a round); the pilot light of 5 is the exit if the row reads cold. No model yet (MechView3D borrows the Badger's); its lowforge model, rig, acts and gait are the asset session's.

passive.name: Thermal Ejection Manifold
passive.description: Its vents blast a random foe for the heat they take off it. Nothing else cools it.

design.fantasy: Ryan's helicarrier: the apex of steampunk-silly military technology, a mobile headquarters on rotors that carries the squad, directs its fire, refuels it and gives it a lift. A butterfly: four wings for four rotors, big, slow, and it carries its load home.
design.niche: The maker's first tier three: a mobile HQ for strategic and tactical support and resupply (Ryan, 20 October: "a helicarrier, a mobile HQ, made for strategic and tactical support, and possible resupply"). It doesn't rain death; it directs units to rain death.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 21 October (the bible's Swallowtail row; the brief retired to git: git show 5d989be:docs/briefs/ws_multirotor.md). The multi-rotor that lent its die (the proposal of 11 October) was reworked on 20 October: the lending was abusable and a boring combo piece; the equipment slots that replaced it were cut the same day (tedious to play and balance). The shape (Ryan, 21 October): a third bar, the Muster, filling a sliver every time any die rolls (about thirty rolls a charge, a kill by its own guns worth five), stored up to a cap, per fight from empty; every locked piece has a plain form, spent any time, and a charged form that consumes a muster: the Mooring Screens (a team shield; Phased on every ally that has not acted), the Spotting Flare (it Exposes a foe; it Exposes and Suppresses, Ryan, 21 October, in the Kestrel session, where nothing on the helicarrier is called Mark), the Sutler's Hoist (a shield and some cooling; the full reset), the Reveille Horn (a team reroll; an ally acts again). The passive's map half is the carry: allies adjacent to it travel with it when it moves, set down on the nearest standable hexes beyond anything they cannot stand on, keeping whatever move and action they had (the lift changes where they are, never what they have left); its move is small on purpose, a bump over a river or a crag, a strategic piece and no movement abuse. Numbers: hull 200, shield 60, armour 5, move 20, heat 80, cooling 10, three hardpoints (a d7), stock the maker's Indirect pieces and a shield, every number a placeholder. Names Claude's on Ryan's pick (the chassis his). Built 21 October: the Muster (static muster: a point for every die that rolls, any machine's, 30 a charge, 5 for each kill by its own guns, up to three charges, the cap a placeholder; a store, so a Silence sleeps it and a Purge takes it), the charged spend (a tap on the carrier arms its die, the die showing the charged form until it is spent), Phased, the team shield, the Hoist's two forms, Rallied and an ally acting again, the Flare's Expose, and the carry on the map (static carry: every machine beside it set down beside where it stops, a stop that cannot seat them refused, an undo taking them back). No model yet (MechView3D borrows the Badger's); a tier three is never a tender's deal.

passive.name: Muster Deck
passive.description: Allies beside it on the map travel with it. Every die that rolls fills its Muster a sliver, a kill by its own guns more, and its locked pieces spend a muster to do more.

design.fantasy: Ryan's mobile artillery, 21 October: "a cross between a Big Bertha, a M270 MLRS, and/or a truck-mounted MEADS launcher. Big. Big wheels. Massive launchers and massive artillery cannons"; the "high-tech" Wainwright & Sutler design, "where they tried to resolve their inherent bias against energy weapons". Wide (Ryan: "Wide is good"): the old cannon on the centreline, the high-tech guns on flank sponsons, a rack of glowing cells feeding them, the musk ox's ring of horns facing out.
design.niche: The maker's second tier three, the old-world artillery and the raining death: the machine that runs on ammo where every other runs on heat, so it carries any maker's hottest energy guns without heating. Its cluster cannon earns ammo off a crowd and lays Flak for the team; its salvo spends the whole magazine at random foes, Spread and Penetrate on every strike.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 21 October (the bible's Musk Ox row; the brief retired to git: git show bc97727:docs/briefs/ws_artillery.md). From the Minerva session's all-shells candidate for the siege battery (17 October), which Ryan read on 20 October as this maker's tier three. The shape is Ryan's; Claude's reading found it inverse heat as first written and kept the three rules heat cannot have: a low start that ramps, a gun that earns ammo by hitting, and a salvo that spends savings. Numbers are placeholders at today's heat scale: a gun pays 1 ammo for every 10 heat (Ryan's 2 at the stock pass's scale, a fifth of today's), so the Thermal Ray's 30 is 3 ammo. Its heat maximum is low on purpose (Ryan: it needs none for its guns, so the quick reload and the foes' heat together are a real threat). Built 21 October: the magazine on the machine (static forge: 10, opening each fight at 3, gaining 1 a round from the second; never a status, so no Silence or Purge reaches it), the conversion read through the pipeline (a damaging gun's own heat, a foe's debuff's extra aside, 1 ammo for every 10, rounded up, at least 1; Scorched's extra and every other kind's heat on the heat bar), the refund, the reloads (a vent on itself 3, a shield 2, the quick reload its own 2 and no vent's), the salvo (every ammo a strike at a random live foe, the magazine its price, no heat), a dry gun unspendable and the die printing each gun's price; the bar under the heat. No model yet (MechView3D borrows the Badger's); a tier three is never a tender's deal.

passive.name: Desublimation Forge
passive.description: Its damaging guns fire forged ammo instead of heating it: 1 for every 10 heat a gun would make, rounded up, at least 1. The forge makes 1 each round; a vent it spends on itself adds 3, a shield 2.

design.fantasy: Ryan's bomber (14 and 15 October): soft control that traps a slot so a reinforcement comes in damaged, "a bomber of some kind", its bombs taking on the properties of its weapons. The weapon is the bomb: any weapon may be spent on an empty slot and its keywords ride in the mine. The bearded vulture carries bones and tortoises up and drops them to shatter on rock (Ryan named it 21 October): a heavy tandem-wing flyer on big boosters, a pair of wings fore and a pair aft, the mines dropping from the bay between.
design.niche: Kestrel's tier-three minelayer: the lowest floor and the highest ceiling. With reinforcements waiting it is an engine, every arrival paying before it acts (a stun mine takes its first action, a burn mine ticks on it, a shock mine doubles the team's first blow); with nothing waiting a plain d6 flyer whose laid mines the Lorentz Contractor cashes on a chosen foe. It wants keyword weapons of every maker and the team's killers, the Syrinx Drone copying the best killing shot onto the next arrival.
design.notes: Ryan's go, 21 October, on the design settled in chat from 14 to 21 October (the brief retired to git: git show 62192a4:docs/briefs/kestrel_bomber.md; the bible's Kestrel row carries the decisions and their reasons). Ryan's names: the Lammergeier (the Magpie until that evening), the Fuse-delayed Bay, the Lorentz Contractor, the Syrinx Drone; the designation is Claude's on his word. Every number is a placeholder (a heavy flyer at Kestrel's pace, move 40; hull 110, shield 70, armour 0, heat 80, cooling 5, recharge 25; four hardpoints beside the two locks, a d6). The stock is stand-ins by kind until the stock pass, keyword pieces so the stock shows the bombs: the Incendiary Shells (napalm), the Enfilade Beam (a column mine, Penetrate, standing in for the kit's Spread piece, since no Spread weapon is free to stock today), the Polarity Projector (a shock mine), the Arc Fault Cannon (Kestrel's lightning mine, Chain living in mines). The engine was built 21 October: an empty slot as a target, the mine store carried by the save, the landing once the reinforcement step has placed every arrival, left to right, any other way in (a Swap) setting it off at once, every keyword acting as on a blow (Chain repeating its spender's attack, Lure and Disrupt inert), the pull and the drone as printed rules, and the bot's value of a mine. No model yet (MechView3D borrows the Badger's); its lowforge model, rig, acts and the heavy flyer's swell are the asset session's.

passive.name: Fuse-delayed Bay
passive.description: Its weapons may be spent on an empty slot in the enemy's formation, as if a foe stood there. The shot waits there, and whoever steps in takes every shot waiting, in laid order, before it acts.
